overview.title: Introduction
overview.subtitle: Start here
overview.description: Control an animation’s timing, inspect every update, and connect motion to any layer of your application.

install.title: Installation
install.subtitle: Install the core and create your first instance.
install.description: RxJS is a peer dependency. During source development, the playground resolves the library through Vite’s @lib alias. Consumer applications install the published package as @re-code/flux.

animation.title: One animation, one playhead
animation.subtitle: Animation controls time; your application decides which properties to render.
animation.description: An instance tracks normalized progress, resolves easing, and emits lifecycle callbacks. This demo uses those values to update position, rotation, and opacity in real time.

parameters.title: Parameters
parameters.subtitle: Options are fixed when an instance is created.
parameters.description: Options are immutable after creation. To change duration, delay, or easing, stop the animation and create a new instance.

timing-examples.title: Delay, repeat & yoyo
timing-examples.subtitle: Try each parameter and see how it changes the animation clock.
timing-examples.description: Delay postpones the active start. Repeat counts additional repeats, and yoyo reverses progress on alternating cycles. Apply options to create a new instance.

controls.title: Methods and callbacks
controls.subtitle: Chainable controls for managing the full lifecycle.
controls.description: The API also provides onStart, onComplete, onPause, onResume, and onStop. They run when the corresponding state transition occurs, not when the instance is created.

callback-examples.title: Live callbacks
callback-examples.subtitle: Callbacks describe transitions; you do not need to log an event on every frame.
callback-examples.description: This log listens for onStart, onPause, onResume, onStop, and onComplete. The onUpdate callback moves the box without flooding the log with dozens of entries per second.

timeline.title: Timeline
timeline.subtitle: Coordinates multiple animations on a shared timeline.
timeline.description: A Timeline coordinates its children using global time and moves them with seekLocal(ms). Entries can overlap or rewind without creating a separate loop for each child.

offsets.title: Timeline offsets
offsets.subtitle: Express sequence timing without manual timestamp arithmetic.
offsets.description: An omitted offset appends after the previous item. Numeric offsets are absolute; +=, -= and < express relative, overlapping, or parallel timing.

offset-explorer.title: Compare offsets
offset-explorer.subtitle: Change the offset and inspect how the segments line up.
offset-explorer.description: The chart is built from Timeline.segments, so the visual layout reflects the same timing model used by the runtime.

nested-timeline.title: Nested timelines & composition helpers
nested-timeline.subtitle: Compose a timeline inside another timeline.
nested-timeline.description: Nest timelines when building larger scenes, or use sequence(), parallel(), and staggered() to compose reusable AnimatableItems without manually calculating every offset.

reactivity.title: Reactive state
reactivity.subtitle: Progress and state are first-class RxJS streams.
reactivity.description: Subscribe to progress$ and state$ to connect animations to application state. Remember to unsubscribe when the consumer no longer needs updates.

await-example.title: Await completion
await-example.subtitle: Animation and Timeline are thenable.
await-example.description: Await resolves when the active cycle completes and rejects if the cycle is stopped before completion. Use try/finally for cleanup.

easings.title: Easings
easings.subtitle: Resolve a curve by name or pass a custom function.
easings.description: Easing transforms normalized progress. The animation engine remains responsible for time; the easing function only shapes how progress maps to a value.

easing-gallery.title: Compare easing curves
easing-gallery.subtitle: Compare curves and inspect their effect on a moving value.
easing-gallery.description: Elastic and bounce curves can overshoot or reverse direction. Use unclamped progress when that behavior is part of the desired motion.

retarget-motion.title: Retarget motion streams
retarget-motion.subtitle: Change a target without resetting current position and velocity.
retarget-motion.description: retargetMotion() consumes a stream of target values and emits samples containing position and velocity while using the shared frame coordinator.

smooth-stream.title: Smooth asynchronous streams
smooth-stream.subtitle: Interpolate timestamped values using a bounded latency buffer.
smooth-stream.description: smoothStream() handles irregular arrivals by rendering behind the newest available input. Late samples that fall behind the output cursor are ignored instead of moving time backwards.

adaptive-tween.title: Adaptive tweening
adaptive-tween.subtitle: Adjust transition duration to match incoming data cadence.
adaptive-tween.description: adaptiveTween() estimates the interval between accepted timestamps and adapts each transition duration. It preserves the rendered value during retargeting, but does not preserve physical velocity.

render-adapters.title: Headless render adapters
render-adapters.subtitle: Connect value streams to browser rendering without importing renderer bindings into the core.
render-adapters.description: Optional subpaths expose DOM styles, SVG attributes, Canvas 2D drawing and structural Three.js transforms. These adapters are opt-in and remain outside the headless core.

keyframes-dom.title: Keyframes & DOM targets
keyframes-dom.subtitle: Define typed value sequences in the headless core, or opt into selector-based CSS animation from the DOM entry point.
keyframes-dom.description: keyframes() returns a reusable Keyframes<T> animatable item. Offsets are normalized from 0 to 1; missing offsets are distributed between known offsets, and each frame can set the easing for its outgoing segment.

gesture-physics.title: Production-grade gesture physics
gesture-physics.subtitle: Treat pointer input as a lifecycle, not just a stream of coordinates.
gesture-physics.description: pointerGestures$ captures the active pointer when supported, observes release and cancellation outside the element, and cancels safely when capture is lost, the window blurs, or the document becomes hidden. dragInertia applies axis locking, filtered velocity in units per second, dynamic bounds, and stops outward velocity at a hard edge. Unsubscribe to release capture and all listeners.

motion-lifecycle.title: Motion preferences & lifecycle
motion-lifecycle.subtitle: Reduce motion and pause hidden-page work per instance.
motion-lifecycle.description: MotionPreferences observes prefers-reduced-motion and document visibility. Pass it to a directly played Animation or to the Timeline that controls a composed scene; the parent timeline policy governs its children. Finite motion can jump to its final state, unbounded playback suspends while reduced motion is requested, and pauseWhenHidden pauses/resumes around tab visibility without imposing a global policy.

frame-observability.title: Frame observability & leak diagnostics
frame-observability.subtitle: Measure shared scheduler work and assert teardown in tests.
frame-observability.description: FrameCoordinator publishes frame work duration, rolling averages, maximum work, subscriber counts, queued read/write tasks, and clock state. metrics$ does not itself start the frame loop. getDiagnostics() returns an immutable snapshot; assertIdle() throws with the outstanding work counts when a coordinator still has consumers or scheduled tasks.

scroll-triggers.title: Scroll triggers & scrubbed timelines
scroll-triggers.subtitle: Turn scroll boundaries into lifecycle events and normalized timeline progress.
scroll-triggers.description: createScrollTrigger() supports explicit start/end anchors, directional enter/leave callbacks, refresh after layout changes, and optional Timeline scrubbing. Scroll updates are coalesced through the shared frame coordinator; destroy the controller to remove listeners and pending work.

ui.adapterImplementationNote: DOM, SVG, Canvas and structural Three.js adapters are implemented as opt-in entry points. Canvas pixels are not restored on unsubscribe; configure clearOnUnsubscribe when clearing is desired.
ui.domAnimateEntryNote: Import animate() from @re-code/flux/dom. Call it as animate(targets, options): targets may be a CSS selector, one Element, or an iterable such as an array or NodeList. The options object contains animation-level defaults and a required properties map; put CSS properties inside options.properties, not at the top level. Each property supports a scalar endpoint, an array of values, { from, to }, { values, ...timing }, { keyframes, ...timing }, or a target-aware factory. The returned DOMAnimation is a Timeline; dispose() releases bindings and restores original inline styles.
ui.propertyDefinitionDescription: Define CSS properties inside options.properties, not on the outer options object. A property accepts a scalar endpoint, evenly distributed values, a factory (target, index, total) => values, { from, to }, { values, ...timing }, or { keyframes, ...timing }.
ui.propertyTimingDescription: Top-level duration, delay, easing, repeat, and yoyo provide defaults. A property object can override them. If no global duration is supplied, each property object must define a duration. Global delay, property delay, and target stagger are added together and clamped at time zero.
ui.keyframeOffsetDescription: Offsets are normalized to 0–1. Each keyframe’s easing applies to the segment leading away from that keyframe.
ui.staggerDescription: Adds a per-target delay. Use a number for the delay step, or a callback (index, target, total) => delayMs.
ui.disposeDescription: Cancels active playback if needed, releases style subscriptions and restores original inline declarations.
ui.cssInterpolationDescription: Values with matching numeric templates and units interpolate numerically. Incompatible values change discretely at the endpoint; for transforms, provide explicit arrays whose string templates match.
ui.headlessImportDescription: The headless package has no selector or document dependency. Import keyframes from @re-code/flux for renderer-independent values, and import animate from @re-code/flux/dom only when you need DOM selection and CSS styles.

pipeline.title: The Reactive Pipeline Architecture
pipeline.description: The same motion data can be retargeted, sampled, and consumed by different render targets. Each adapter remains opt-in and cleans up its own bindings.

runtimeTelemetry.title: Measure actual frame-coordinator work
runtimeTelemetry.description: Run a spring sample to observe the coordinator metrics emitted by the running engine. These values describe measured scheduler work, not total browser rendering time or a cross-library benchmark.
runtimeTelemetry.chartAriaLabel: Recent samples of frame coordinator work duration
runtimeTelemetry.chartEmpty: Run the sample to populate the chart with real measurements.
runtimeTelemetry.note: Measurement starts while metrics$ is observed and a frame clock is active. The numbers vary by device, browser, CPU load, and other active subscribers.
runtimeTelemetry.paradigmTitle: Reactive motion as a shared pipeline
runtimeTelemetry.compositionDescription: Compose typed values and operators with RxJS and coordinate multiple items on a shared frame clock.
runtimeTelemetry.renderTargetsDescription: Keep rendering opt-in through DOM, SVG, Canvas and structural Three.js adapters.
runtimeTelemetry.lifecycleDescription: Dispose subscriptions and adapter bindings explicitly; use diagnostics to detect outstanding scheduler work.
runtimeTelemetry.imperativeCompositionDescription: Each animation often owns its own update callbacks and timing logic unless a shared orchestration layer is added.
runtimeTelemetry.imperativeTargetsDescription: Rendering code is commonly tied to a specific element or renderer, which may require separate glue to share values.
runtimeTelemetry.imperativeLifecycleDescription: Listeners and loops need explicit cleanup; a missed teardown can keep work alive past a view lifecycle.
runtimeTelemetry.paradigmNote: This is a qualitative architecture comparison, not a performance ranking. Use the live metrics above and the repository benchmarks to measure concrete workloads.

home.heroTagline: Compose high-framerate animations, reactive event streams, and physical springs with one lightweight, tree-shakable TypeScript engine.

story.title: One unified engine.
story.description: A continuous observable pipeline dissolves the divide between interface mechanics, vector physics, and canvas rendering.

steps.title: Compose Motion
steps.description: Staggered entrances, orchestrated micro-delays, and carefully chosen easing curves let a whole scene move with intention. Build sequences without a maze of nested callbacks.

steps.title: Think Reactively
steps.description: Streams are first-class primitives. Combine changing values and event input, then connect them to DOM or canvas output without burying the animation loop inside rendering code.

steps.title: Feel the Physics
steps.description: Retarget spring motion while it is moving. Position and velocity flow forward, creating physical responses that feel connected to the interaction rather than restarting on every input.

steps.title: Animate beyond interfaces
steps.description: Keep the motion model independent from the renderer. Reuse values and timing for DOM styles, SVG paths, Canvas draw callbacks, and compatible Three.js transforms.

samples.lineOne: const tween = new Tween({ from: 0, to: 1 });

principles.title: Designed for reactive motion. Built to stay composable.
principles.description: Focused primitives keep timing, reactive inputs, rendering, and lifecycle concerns understandable as the scene becomes more ambitious.

items.title: RxJS Stream Native
items.description: Use observable values as first-class inputs and outputs, then compose them using the operators you already know.

items.title: Frame Coordination
items.description: Coordinate animation work around the shared frame scheduler instead of scattering unrelated timing loops.

items.title: Rendering Adapters
items.description: Connect motion to DOM styles, SVG paths, Canvas 2D draw callbacks, and compatible Three.js objects.

items.title: Lifecycle & Cleanup
items.description: Give animations and subscriptions explicit owners, and clean them up deliberately when an experience ends.

visualLab.title: Visual Lab Experiments
visualLab.description: Small, live experiments that turn motion primitives into geometry, pixels, and expressive interactions.

items.title: SVG & Geometry
items.description: Morph paths, reveal vector strokes, and animate motion along curves.

items.title: Canvas & Data
items.description: Particles, waves, and procedural scenes driven frame by frame.

items.title: Kinetic Interactions
items.description: Pointer physics, reactive typography, and responsive motion.

items.title: Scroll motion
items.description: Triggers, normalized progress, and scrubbed timelines.

closing.title: Give your motion a reactive core.
closing.description: Explore the API, experiment in the playgrounds, and build motion that stays understandable as your scenes grow.
